statements.statement_en: Yeshiva students should be drafted into the army or civilian service, even if this forces them to give up full-time Torah study.
Tuition aid, daycare, tax breaks and land should go first to those who did military or national service, even if others get less.
Israel should restrict more strictly the entry and residence of foreigners, including citizens' spouses who come from the Palestinian territories, even if this separates some families.
Israel should reduce the number of foreign workers, even if construction, agriculture and elderly care become more expensive.
Getting a divorce should be easier, even if one of the spouses objects.
Suspects and defendants should have fewer legal protections during arrest, questioning and trial, even if the risk of convicting innocent people grows.
Prosecutors should be able to investigate and try a sitting prime minister or minister, even if this removes an elected leader before any verdict.
Teachers, lecturers and public employees who express support for terrorism should be dismissed, even without a criminal conviction.
